topic.title: Parents who want the ban, on their own phones
topic.claim: Everyone wants teenagers off Instagram, but nobody asked what the adults would do with the hours.
topic.behaviour: Parents backing an under-18 social media ban while scrolling through dinner. Teens opening accounts anyway.
topic.mechanism: A ban lets adults hand off a worry they can't model themselves. Moral panic is cheaper than changing your own habit.
real_details: The Centre reportedly told the Supreme Court on 28 September it would amend the IT Rules so under-18s can't open accounts on their own
Karnataka announced an under-16 ban in March
There is no nationwide ban yet and the amended rules had not been published
DPDP parental-consent rules for children's data are due from May 2027
topic.news_peg: Centre's reported statement to the Supreme Court on 28 September 2026 about amending the IT Rules
topic.why_now: The proposal is being debated and nothing is final, so the argument is live at home.

score.reason: live SC debate gives a fresh event hook, and the hypocrisy angle is sharp and arguable
score.best_hook: Parents want Instagram banned for 16-year-olds. The same parents haven't put their phone down at dinner in years.

sources.fact: Reporting on the Supreme Court hearing of 28 September 2026 says the Centre, through Solicitor General Tushar Mehta, agreed to examine safeguards for minors. The bench asked it to consider putting the requirement into the statutory intermediary rules, and no firm commitment to amend them is quoted.
sources.excerpt: "Something can be done, something should be done and will be done. We have to come back…" "Not a request, a direction," Mehta said.

sources.fact: A LocalCircles survey reported by PTI in September 2023 found 61% of urban Indian parents said their children aged 9-17 spend about three or more hours a day on social media, videos/OTT and online games. 73% wanted mandatory parental consent for under-18 users.
sources.excerpt: "61 per cent of urban Indian parents of children between ages 9-17 conceded" that their children spend roughly three or more hours a day on these platforms, with "spend an average of three hours or more each day on social media, videos/OTT and online games." "73 per cent of urban Indian parents surveyed want the data protection law to ensure mandatory parental consent" for users under 18. "35 per cent indicated that their children spent the most time on social media," "The survey received over 46,000 responses from urban Indian parents located in 296 districts."
